title: Begin from the Third Story
coreMove: Start from a neutral description of the gap between views and invite comparison rather than defense.
sourcePressure: The chapter has one main move: replace first-story openers with a third-story opener plus genuine invitation.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Softening an accusation while leaving your story as the baseline.

sourceAnchors.name: third story opener
sourceAnchors.detail: The source defines the third story as a neutral-observer account that names the disagreement without making either side the defendant.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A third-story opener gives both people a view of the gap before either one has to defend a character.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.

hook: Do not open ch08 with a generic dread-before-meeting frame
Do not begin with a definition of the chapter term
Do not use a negotiation-table abstraction as the first image
counterintuition: Avoid the shell 'you think X, but actually Y'
Avoid claiming the idea is simply counterintuitive
Avoid treating compassion as the surprising twist
tryThisNow: No 'pause and reflect on your communication style' action
examples: Avoid repeated coffee-table, classroom, narrow-kitchen, bus-depot, marker, mug, or radiator shells
Avoid six workplace meetings with changed names
Avoid making every case a manager feedback scene

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: use these six opening devices in order: second-person You direct address; sensory detail first; timestamp+name+action; dialogue first line; environmental detail before any human; retrospective first line
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: separated parents trying not to make the other a defendant
exampleSpecs.stakes: their child is hearing contradictory responses after tantrums
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily rewrites 'you are undermining me' into a sentence about different ideas of what the tantrum needs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a child's rain boots by the front door

exampleSpecs.audience: consultants with competing versions of a failed transfer
exampleSpecs.stakes: a client renewal depends on stopping the defensive spiral early
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lukas opens with two teams working from different handoff assumptions, then invites notes comparison
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a conference badge lanyard on a hotel table

exampleSpecs.domain: graduate student approaching advisor about delayed feedback
exampleSpecs.stakes: a thesis timeline is slipping and the power gap makes a summons risky
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta writes an opener the advisor could recognize without accepting all of it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I think we may be using different timelines," she says

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant partners disagreeing on tip pooling
exampleSpecs.audience: small business partners with identity and fairness stakes
exampleSpecs.stakes: staff trust could break if the policy change starts as an accusation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chris names the gap between fairness assumptions before proposing a policy debate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tip envelope sealed with blue tape

exampleSpecs.audience: families where history sits under logistics
exampleSpecs.stakes: a roof repair decision could reopen old roles if the opener blames one sibling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Adaeze tests whether Antoine would recognize the third-story version before calling
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a roofer's estimate folded in thirds

exampleSpecs.domain: open-source maintainers reviewing a rejected pull request
exampleSpecs.audience: online collaborators with public defensiveness risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: the contributor may leave if the opening frames them as careless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Antoine begins with different assumptions about review readiness rather than with the rejection itself
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pull request page with failing checks

skillTargets: identify when a scenario needs start from a neutral description of the gap between views and invite comparison rather than defense.
distinguish first story from the adjacent generic misread
choose the visible action that demonstrates the chapter move rather than merely naming it
explain why the wrong option would recreate softening an accusation while leaving your story as the baseline.

tryThisNowSpec: Draft a third-story opener that the other person could recognize as plausible even while disagreeing with your view.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
